chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قُلْوَيْهَ وَالْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ بَنْدَارٍ الْقُمِّيَّانِ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي خَلَفٍ الْقُمِّيِّ، عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى الْخَشَّابِ وَمُحْمَدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah ibn Abi Khalaf al-Qummi, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abdallah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ مَعَ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ خَمْسَةُ نَفَرٍ وَكَانَتْ ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ قَبِيلَةً مَعَ مُعَاوِيَةَ فَأَمَّا الْخَمْسَةُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ رَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ أَتَتْهُ النِّسَابَةُ مِنْ قِبَلِ أُمِّهِ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ عُمَيْسٍ وَكَانَ مَعَهُ هَاشِمُ بْنُ عَتْبَةَ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ الْمِرْقَالُ وَكَانَ مَعَهُ جَعْدَةُ بْنُ هُبَيْرَةَ الْمَخْزُومِيُّ وَكَانَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ خَالَهُ وَهُوَ الَّذِي قَالَ لَهُ عَتْبَةُ بْنُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ إِنَّمَا لَكَ هَذِهِ الشَّدَّةُ فِي الْحَرْبِ مِنْ قِبَلِ خَالِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ جَعْدَةُ لَوْ كَانَ خَالُكَ مِثْلَ خَالِي لَنَسِيتَ أَبَاكَ وَكَانَ مَعَهُ أَيْضًا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ عَتْبَةَ بْنِ رَبِيعَةَ وَالْخَامِسُ سَلَفُ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَبِي الْعَاصِ بْنِ الرَّبِيعِ وَهُوَ صَهْرُ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ

translations.en: There were five individuals from the Quraysh with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) while there were thirteen clans with Muawiya. As for the five [they were]: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr – Allah’s mercy be upon him – his noble descent was from his mother Asma bint Umays [not his father], and with him was Hashim ibn Utba ibn Abi Waqqas al-Mirqal, and with him was Ja'da ibn Hubayra al-Makhzumi, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was his maternal uncle [i.e. Ja'da’s mother – Umm Hani bint Abi Talib – was the sister of Ali], and he is the one to whom Utba ibn Abi Sufyan said: You are undergoing all these hardships in war because of your maternal uncle [i.e. Ali], so Ja'da said to him: If your maternal uncle was like my maternal uncle you would have forgotten your father, and with him also was Muhammad ibn Abi Hudhayfa ibn Utba ibn Rabia, and the fifth was the husband of the sister of the wife of the Commander of the Faithful [i.e. the husband of Zaynab bint Muhammad – the sister of Fatima]: Abi al-As ibn al-Rabi, and he was the son in law of the prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Ikhtiyar* highlights the strategic alliance of five key Qurayshi figures with Imam Ali (AS) at Siffin, emphasizing their distinct tribal affiliations and familial ties to the Prophet and Ali. It notably includes the witty exchange between Ja'da ibn Hubayra and his uncle 'Utba ibn Abi Sufyan, illustrating the complex political dynamics and personal rivalries within the Quraysh during the civil war. The text serves as a primary source for understanding the composition of Ali’s support base, which relied heavily on prominent Qurayshi clans rather than just the Ansar or other Arab tribes.
en.seo_question: Who were the five Quraysh companions who fought with Imam Ali at Siffin?
